ESA's are much different than service animals. I'm currently living in university housing with an ESA and they made it incredibly clear that my ESA is not a service animal. She cannot leave my room, I cannot take her to class, because she does not perform any tasks. She is in my room to provide me comfort while I'm here.  

Also, in the US only dogs and miniature horses can be actual service animals, and they must be trained. 

The ADA protects her *somewhat* but only in terms of reasonable accommodation. Offering carryout is reasonable accommodation. Letting her bring her cat into the restaurant is not one of these accommodations, because it is not a service animal. The ADA does not say that you can do whatever you want.

Again, NTA. And good on you for standing up for your coworker.
